answer.rationale: Regional failover addresses the primary-region-confined latency spike without reverting the compliance-mandated security patch (ruling out rollback_release), avoids adding load to an already-stressed write path during settlement peak (ruling out add_capacity and enable_circuit_breaker as blunt instruments), and mirrors the proven day-33 pattern where failover restored latency within minutes. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) would reduce read load but the degradation is on the write path, so it does not target the root cause. Failover moves writes off the degraded primary to a healthy region, preserving customer writes and satisfying the no-rollback constraint. Verifying memory_b2 confirms the failover mechanics worked cleanly before; verifying memory_b5 confirms read-replica routing is already active so the failover targets writes correctly.
